subject.title: Update to 2026.7.1 left managed install and WhatsApp plugin linked to old embedded Node

question: Should a local-prefix `openclaw update` automatically hand off to the hosted installer when the target release requires a newer embedded Node, or stop before package mutation and direct the user through a managed recovery flow?
rationale: Core currently owns package/plugin/service update behavior while the hosted installer owns the embedded Node toolchain, so a maintainer must confirm the supported cross-repository handoff and rollback contract before implementation.

options.title: Atomic installer handoff
options.body: Detect the managed prefix, upgrade the embedded runtime through the installer, then complete core, plugin, and service convergence as one verified operation.

options.title: Fail before mutation
options.body: Preflight the Node floor and leave the existing installation untouched while presenting a visible installer recovery action and exact diagnostic.

recommendation.title: Atomic installer handoff
recommendation.body: Detect the managed prefix, upgrade the embedded runtime through the installer, then complete core, plugin, and service convergence as one verified operation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail covers both updater install-root repair and the sibling local-prefix installer topology.
